title: React Internals Applied Check
description: Apply React internals knowledge to state preservation, render purity, commit timing, refs, concurrent rendering, stale closures, automatic batching, flushSync, and Strict Mode edge cases.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A list uses array indexes as keys, then users reorder items and input values appear under the wrong rows. What explains this?

options.text: React matched children by unstable positions, so state was preserved for the wrong logical item
React cannot render input elements in lists

questions.explanation: Keys represent identity. Index keys break down when items are inserted, removed, or reordered.

questions.prompt: A component calls `analytics.track()` directly in the component body. Why is this risky?

options.text: Render can run more than once or be discarded, so side effects do not belong there
The browser cannot send analytics from React apps
React requires class components for analytics

questions.explanation: Render must be pure. Side effects should run in effects or event handlers so React can safely render, retry, or discard work.

questions.prompt: Inside one click handler, code calls `setCount(count + 1); setCount(count + 1);`. Starting from 0, why might the result be 1 instead of 2?

options.text: Both updates read the same stale `count` from the current render
React ignores the second setter forever

questions.explanation: Both updates capture the same value. Use functional updates like `setCount(c => c + 1)` when next state depends on previous state.

questions.prompt: Which operations belong after commit rather than during render? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reading or writing DOM layout through refs
Returning JSX based only on props and state

questions.explanation: DOM refs, subscriptions, timers, and other side effects happen after React commits, usually in effects or layout effects.

questions.prompt: If concurrent rendering starts rendering a tree and later discards it, effects from that discarded render should have already run.
questions.explanation: Effects run after commit. Work that never commits should not run commit-phase effects.

questions.prompt: A heavy search update makes typing feel slow. Which React tool can mark that update as lower priority?

options.text: A random key on the input

questions.explanation: Transitions let urgent updates such as input text stay responsive while non-urgent rendering can be deferred.

options.text: Rarely, when code truly needs React to flush DOM updates synchronously before continuing
Around every state update for better performance

questions.explanation: flushSync is an escape hatch. Overusing it fights React's scheduler and can hurt performance.

questions.prompt: Strict Mode mounts, unmounts, and remounts an effect in development and a duplicate subscription appears. What is missing?

options.text: A cleanup function that unsubscribes correctly

questions.explanation: Strict Mode exposes effects that do not clean up after themselves, such as subscriptions, sockets, or timers.
